How Much Does It Cost to Renovate a Bathroom in Toronto in 2026?

Real 2026 CAD price ranges for a bathroom renovation in Toronto: full gut renovations, mid-range refreshes, plumbing and tiling costs, and how Toronto compares to the rest of Ontario.

Sommario

  1. Toronto bathroom renovation costs by tier
  2. Where the money goes
  3. Toronto vs. the rest of Ontario and Canada

Bathroom renovations are consistently one of the highest-value projects homeowners take on, and one of the widest-ranging in price. In Toronto specifically, labour costs and permit requirements push totals higher than the national average. Here's a realistic breakdown for 2026.

Toronto bathroom renovation costs by tier

  • Cosmetic refresh (new vanity, toilet, fixtures, paint — no plumbing moves): $8,000–$14,000
  • Mid-range renovation (new tile, tub-to-shower conversion, vanity, lighting): $18,000–$32,000
  • Full gut renovation (moved plumbing, custom shower, heated floors, premium finishes): $35,000–$60,000+

For a standard 5x8 ft bathroom, most Toronto homeowners land between $16,000 and $28,000 for a genuine mid-range renovation that touches plumbing, tile, and fixtures.

Where the money goes

  • Plumbing (rough-in changes, new supply lines, drain work): $2,500–$8,000
  • Tiling (floor and shower walls, labour and materials): $3,500–$9,000
  • Vanity and countertop: $800–$4,500
  • Shower/tub: $1,500–$8,000 depending on custom glass and tile work
  • Electrical (potlights, exhaust fan, GFCI outlets): $800–$2,500
  • Permits and inspections: $200–$800 in most Toronto-area municipalities when plumbing or electrical is altered

Toronto vs. the rest of Ontario and Canada

Toronto and the GTA typically run 20–30% above smaller Ontario markets like London, Kitchener-Waterloo, or Windsor for comparable scope, driven largely by trade labour rates and permit turnaround. Compared nationally, Vancouver runs similarly high to Toronto, while Calgary, Edmonton, and Winnipeg tend to be 10–20% lower. Quebec markets, including Montreal, are often the most affordable of Canada's major metros for the same renovation scope.

Common cost surprises

Hidden water damage

Older Toronto homes (especially pre-1980s builds) often reveal subfloor rot or outdated plumbing once tile comes up. Budget a 10–15% contingency for this — it's one of the most common reasons a bathroom renovation quote changes mid-project.

Moving the toilet or shower drain

Relocating a drain, even by a foot, can add $1,500–$4,000 depending on whether the home is on a concrete slab or has an accessible basement below.

Custom glass showers

Frameless glass enclosures look great but run $1,200–$3,500 installed, compared to $300–$700 for a standard sliding door or curtain setup.

How to compare quotes properly

A trustworthy bathroom renovation quote should break out plumbing, tiling, electrical, fixtures, and labour as separate line items — not one lump sum. It should also state whether permits are included and who is responsible for pulling them. Contractors using AI quoting tools built for tradespeople can generate this level of detail directly from a site visit, which makes comparing multiple quotes far easier for homeowners.
